sections.content: How many people are "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists"?

25,910 people

were counted on the census as "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists use a variety of therapies in one-on-one or group settings to help people with mental health issues, stress, emotional and relationship problems.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists", 15.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists" included:

  • clergy
  • bus and coach drivers
  • garage managers and proprietors

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists" there were more women than men (79.6% compared with 20.4%).

This means "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 20.4% and women made up 79.6% of "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists" included:

  • librarians
  • counsellors
  • hairdressing and beauty salon managers and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists", 14.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (60.4% compared with 39.6%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (57.4%) than an employee (42.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Camden, this is in the same region of London.
